newsitem.title: UK: Two UK ministers say May 1 preferred election date.
newsitem.headline: Two UK ministers say May 1 preferred election date.

text.p: Two senior cabinet ministers said on Friday that Prime Minister John Major's preferred date for the general election was May 1.

Speaking after newspaper speculation that Major might opt for an earlier electoral contest, Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine and Defence Secretary Michael Portillo said they would be happy to hold on until May.
"John Major has suggested that May 1 may be his preferred date. That seems fine to me," Portillo told reporters during a visit to Scotland.
And Heseltine, asked whether an election was likely then during a visit to Bolton, northern England, replied: "That is the Prime Minister's preferred date."
"The Prime Minister has indicated a preference for going full-time and we can't see any reason why we shouldn't do that," he added.
